title: Soft-launch routing workflow and hypotheses (personal notebook)
content:
Quick brain-dump / working plan for a soft launch that focuses on routing-tier experiments and early-signal validation. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, partial, TODOs.

Background / why this exists:
- We want a controlled way to expose new model variant and routing logic (region-aware + warm-cache preference) without full canary complexity.
- Aim: prove no regression on P95 latency and safety signal count for the selected cohort, while validating cost delta and cache-warmup benefit.

Primary goal:
- Soft-launch to 2–5% of global traffic (by client cohort) routed through new routing service (router-v2) + model v1.2-quant.
- Observe latency, error rate, safety flags, token cost per request, and KV cache hit rate over 48–72h.

Secondary goals / hypotheses to test:
1) Hypothesis A: router-v2 preferring warm cache nodes reduces mean tokens-per-request CPU by ~6–10% for short-session cohorts (avg seq len < 128).
   - Signal: cache_hit_rate (prefix), median token execution time per request down.
2) Hypothesis B: region-aware fanout will reduce cross-region tail latency but may increase overall infra cost by ~3%.
   - Signal: p95 latency by region, egress bytes, cost-estimate tagging.
3) Hypothesis C: pinning model version at route level reduces noisy rollbacks; but initial errors will be higher until warmup completes.

Cohort selection (mapped to client ids):
- Warm cohort (0.5%): high-frequency clients with long sessions (to maximize cache warmup). IDs: client_omega, client_hyperion (placeholder).
- Main soft cohort (2–4%): randomly sampled mid-frequency clients across EU/NA/APAC.
- Control cohort: comparable clients on current router-v1 + model v1.1.

Routing plan (stepwise):
1) Preflight (manual checks, no traffic): deploy router-v2 behind a feature flag; run synthetic load for 2h.
   - smoke commands: curl /health, curl /predict with short prompt, verify KV cache events in logs.
2) Enable warm cohort with stable 0.5% traffic and strict telemetry (extra sampling). Observe 6h.
3) Ramp to 2% by adding more sampled clients (gradual over 1h increments: 0.5 -> 1.0 -> 2.0). Pause 30–60m between ramps to evaluate signals.
4) If stable at 2% for 24h, optionally bump to 4% as extra validation window.
5) Keep control cohort running in parallel.

Quick checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Canary config added to router ruleset (PR merged: github PR/5821).
- [ ] Pager duty runbook updated with new thresholds and contact list.
- [ ] Cohort list finalized and exported to traffic-svc (CSV).
- [ ] Billing tag applied to router-v2 to separate cost metrics.
- [ ] KMS key validated for private logs.
- [ ] QA smoke tests passing on synthetic and sample real traces.

Telemetry & dashboards (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 per region and global. (Primary fail: p95 > baseline + 50ms sustained for 15m)
- Error rate: 5xx and internal model errors. (Primary fail: +0.5% absolute increase in error rate vs control sustained 10m)
- Safety flags: new model safety triggers (chat_nsfw, hallucination_score). (Primary fail: any safety flag > control by 10%)
- Cache metrics: prefix_cache_hit_ratio, kv_fetch_latencies.
- Cost signals: tokens_per_request, infra_cost_estimate (tagged).
- User-perceived latency: client-side xhr metrics for top cohorts.

Abort / rollback triggers (hard and soft):
- Hard: any SEV with user impact (downtime), or safety flag spike > 3x baseline during soft window. Immediate rollback.
- Soft: p95 increase > baseline + 100ms for 30m OR error delta +1% for 30m. Pause ramp and investigate.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Flip router feature flag to route cohort back to router-v1 (automated toggle).
2) Re-run quick smoke tests.
3) Open postmortem stub and tag relevant owners.
4) If root cause is infra (node oom/eviction), trigger infra runbook.

Warmup strategy (to reduce noisy regressions):
- Seed warm cohort with synthetic requests for 2h before traffic begins (script: tools/warmup/seed_kv.sh).
- For high-value clients, prefetch likely prompt prefixes where possible.
- Gradual model weight ramping: allow router to send 50% of requests that are cache-eligible to warm nodes for first 12h.

Experiment notes / ideas to try if stable:
- A/B routing policy: test round-robin vs. lgc-cost heuristic for node selection.
- Weighted routing by cost: prefer lower-cost nodes for background workload.
- Burst window trimming: short-circuit expensive fallback paths during known quiet hours.

Ops comms and stakeholders:
- On-call SRE: Luis Gomez (primary), backup: Samir Khan.
- PM: Maya Patel (product owner).
- Notify channel: #releases-soft-launch, #sre-incidents for paging.
- Weekly sync: Thu 11am PT during rollout window.

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve before ramping beyond 2%):
- Do we have granular cost attribution per router invocation for mixed-node traffic? (Check with finance tagging)
- Are there client SDKs that will break if response latency spikes slightly (old HTTP timeouts)? Need to consult support logs.
- How to quantify user-perceived quality delta for non-chat generation endpoints?

Next immediate tasks (my TODOs):
- [ ] Finalize cohort CSV and handoff to traffic-svc (Ava).
- [ ] Add guardrails to the feature flag with backoff (Luis to add automatic pause on threshold).
- [ ] Wire up extra debug logging for first 2h of warm cohort (Samir).
- [ ] Draft brief for PM + legal about safety telemetry retention (Maya).

Notes to self:
- Keep ramps slow. Most regressions are noisy during warmup and will settle if cache warms; avoid knee-jerk rollbacks unless safety or real user errors present.
- Save a copy of the first 6h span of traces (s3://redwood-inference/soft-launch/avachen/).
- Expect infra cost blip on day 1; quantify and communicate to PM before any further ramp.

References / links (placeholder):
- Soft launch playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/soft-launch-playbook
- Traffic router runbook: runbook:traffic-router-v2
- PR with router changes: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5821
- Jira ticket for this experiment: RINF-4123

End of scratchpad. Update as I get feedback or we run the first warm cohort.
